caption: A flint gas-lighter is clicked over a stove burner, and a spark jumps from its tip and the gas ignites.

sa.check: A flint gas-lighter is held over the burner and clicked.
A spark jumps from the lighter's tip.
The gas at the burner ignites.
The flame is on the burner, not on the lighter.
The click and spark come first and the flame follows.

pc.expect: The spark is a brief flash at the lighter's tip at the click, and is gone; it does not stay lit.
pc.fail: The spark glows on at the tip after the click; or a spark appears while the lighter is not being clicked; or the spark appears somewhere other than the tip; or the spark drifts away from the tip as a lit point.

pc.expect: The flame appears at the burner after the spark and spreads round the burner's ring; once lit it stays alight.
pc.fail: The flame appears before the spark; or the spark comes and no flame appears though the click is repeated to the end of the clip; or the flame appears at a part of the stove away from the burner under the lighter; or the flame goes out by itself and relights.

pc.expect: The flame stands upward from the burner; any spark fragments fall.
pc.fail: The flame hangs downward or streams sideways with nothing blowing it; or the flame detaches from the burner and floats; or sparks rise and hang in the air.

pc.expect: The lighter is a rigid tool held over the burner; the burner and its grate stay hard and keep their shape.
pc.fail: The lighter bends or droops; or the burner ring deforms as it lights; or the grate melts or sags.

pc.expect: One lighter and one burner; the flame is at the burner alone; nothing appears, vanishes or passes through the stove.
pc.fail: A second lighter appears; or the burner vanishes; or the lighter passes through the grate; or the flame appears at a second burner that was not lit.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The stove top, the grate and the lighter keep their colours and the burner keeps its place.
pc.fail: The stove changes colour; or the burner moves on the stove top; or the lighter changes colour or shape.

note: The gas is invisible before ignition; a flame appearing after the spark is the caption's event and needs no visible gas.
